READING: The fresh confirmatory specialists (pi_A2 vs unchanged Pole A, pi_B2 vs the properly-powered, scripted-probe-certified Pole B2/B2-1) did not produce complementary learned specialization. Both deltas are negative in point estimate on BOTH poles, though neither confidence interval statistically confirms a reversal (both include zero) -- the honest description is a null result with a negative lean, not a decisively confirmed reversal like the earlier exploratory arm's. The raw pattern is nonetheless informative: both policies perform noticeably better against Pole B2 than against Pole A regardless of which one was trained for which (0.91-0.93 vs 0.70-0.77), and on each pole the OFF-pole specialist does as well or slightly better than the ON-pole one. This is the same qualitative pattern the exploratory arm's behavioral diagnostic found (general policy-quality differences dominating over situational specialization) -- but now observed under a COMPLETELY DIFFERENT, independently-certified pole construction (B2-1 rather than canonical OP7), which is evidence the difficulty is not specific to the original Pole-B defect this whole C2 track was built to fix.
WHAT_THIS_MEANS_FOR_THE_C2_TRACK: the scripted-probe-level fix (B2-1's defender-lock repair, properly powered at n=192) worked exactly as intended -- G_A and G_B2 both passed cleanly. That was necessary but evidently not sufficient: the environment demonstrably admits complementary scripted strategies, but PPO training at 4v4 did not discover complementary policies from it, on this attempt. This is the SAME two-part diagnosis structure the exploratory arm faced (probe defect vs. training/generalization limits) resolving to the SECOND explanation once the first was fixed.
STATUS_OF_4V4_FOR_THIS_PAPER: per the standing no-second-attempt discipline used everywhere in this program (exploratory arm's closed FAIL, the B2 ladder's first-to-pass rule, every other confirmatory gate): this was the one frozen, prospectively-designed confirmatory attempt for the C2 construction, and it did not pass. Under that discipline, 4v4 now has TWO independently-certified pole constructions (original GUARD_DISTRIBUTED_V2 and this C2/B2-1 redesign) that both failed to produce learned specialist crossover, despite the SECOND construction's scripted-probe demand being properly powered and cleanly confirmed. This is a substantive finding in its own right -- it shifts the open question from 'is the pole definition broken' (now answered: no, not this time) to 'does 4v4 team size structurally limit PPO's ability to discover complementary strategies here' -- and that determination is for PI review, not something this record resolves unilaterally.
